novel_features.name: Operations gap finder
novel_features.description: Find imminent or occupied stays with no cleaning task or missing check-in details.
novel_features.rationale: No single Hostex endpoint returns 'occupied stay lacking a task' — it needs a local join across reservations, tasks, and check-in details.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to catch turnover and check-in problems before a guest complains, instead of eyeballing the calendar.
novel_features.group: Operations: stop problems before guests do

novel_features.name: Stay brief dossier
novel_features.description: One dossier for a single stay: reservation, guest, thread state, tasks, transactions, and review.
novel_features.rationale: Fan-joins every local entity keyed on stay_code into one object, replacing five tab-switches across the app and OTAs.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need the full picture of one stay; to scan many stays for problems use ops-gaps.
novel_features.group: Operations: stop problems before guests do

novel_features.name: Inbox SLA triage
novel_features.description: Rank open guest conversations by age since the last guest message and flag threads past your SLA.
novel_features.rationale: query-conversations returns threads but no age clock; this derives age from the latest-message timestamp and unread_count locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: OTAs penalize slow replies; use this to triage which threads are about to breach SLA.

novel_features.name: Automation preview
novel_features.description: List pending automated messages and reviews and flag any whose thread a human has already handled.
novel_features.rationale: Pending plans alone don't tell you a human already replied; the join to conversation reply-state does.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to vet queued bot actions before they fire on a human-handled thread; for slow human threads use inbox-sla.

novel_features.name: Cross-channel price parity
novel_features.description: Flag property-dates where per-channel listing price or min-stay diverges across channels.
novel_features.rationale: Parity needs N channel listings diffed for the same date; no single Hostex call diffs channels.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to catch silent revenue loss from channel price drift; for availability mismatch use oversell-watch.

novel_features.name: Oversell / double-sell watch
novel_features.description: Flag dates a channel still shows bookable on a property that is blocked or booked on the master calendar.
novel_features.rationale: Master availability vs per-channel inventory is a two-source join the API exposes only separately.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to catch double-sell risk; for price or min-stay drift use price-parity.

novel_features.name: Revenue rollup
novel_features.description: Net income minus expense by property or month over a date range, from the live ledger.
novel_features.rationale: The transactions endpoint requires an explicit start/end date and returns raw entries; this paginates the range and nets them by group and currency in one command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for the Monday portfolio revenue review in one command.

narrative.headline: Every Hostex v3 operation, plus a local SQLite mirror that answers cross-property questions no single Hostex call can — occupancy gaps, revenue rollups, and guest-message SLA, offline.
narrative.value_prop: Hostex has a REST API and an official MCP server but no first-class CLI. This one mirrors all 86 endpoints as typed commands with --json/--select/--dry-run, then syncs reservations, properties, listings, conversations, reviews, tasks and transactions into local SQLite so you can run joins the API can't: which occupied stays have no cleaning task, revenue by property this month, threads unanswered past your SLA, and price-parity gaps across channels. It gets the tricky Hostex plumbing right once: every response is HTTP 200 with error_code in the body, and the multi-layer rate limits return Retry-After.
narrative.auth_narrative: Hostex authenticates with a Hostex-Access-Token header. Create one in the Host Portal (OpenAPI Settings) with read-only or writable scope; tokens do not expire. Set it as HOSTEX_ACCESS_TOKEN. The server also accepts Authorization: Bearer, but prefer the dedicated header. A read-only token rejects every write with error_code 401.

quickstart.comment: Health check; confirms token presence and API reachability without spending a real call.
Pull your reservations and properties into the local SQLite mirror.
Offline full-text search across synced reservations.
Live query with field projection to keep agent context small.

troubleshoots.symptom: Calls return HTTP 200 but nothing works
troubleshoots.fix: Hostex puts the real result in error_code; branch on it, not the HTTP status. error_code 0 means success.

troubleshoots.symptom: "Invalid access token" on the first call
troubleshoots.fix: Check the header spelling Hostex-Access-Token (with the dash) and that HOSTEX_ACCESS_TOKEN is exported.

troubleshoots.symptom: Writes fail with error_code 401 though the token is valid
troubleshoots.fix: Your token is read-only scope. Create a writable token in the Host Portal; scope cannot be changed after creation.
Rate limit hit (per-token, per-endpoint, or per-thread). Back off for the seconds in the Retry-After header.
Account/subscription problem (expired, or Basic edition using a Pro feature). Only the host can fix it in the portal; do not retry.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when an agent or script needs to read or mutate a Hostex host's data: triaging the guest inbox, querying reservations by date/property/status, pushing price/inventory/restriction updates across channels, scheduling cleaning tasks, or rolling up revenue. It is the right tool when the question spans multiple entities (stays + tasks + transactions) because the local SQLite mirror answers those joins offline; a single REST call cannot.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to build a multi-tenant SaaS that acts on behalf of many hosts — that needs the OAuth 2.0 partner flow, not a single access token.
Do not use it as a real-time webhook receiver; it manages webhook subscriptions but does not host an inbound endpoint.
Do not use it to bulk-message guests faster than the per-thread throttle allows; channel OTAs will suspend the account.

recipes.explanation: Reservation payloads are large and deeply nested; --select narrows to the fields an agent needs so it doesn't burn context.

recipes.explanation: After sync, full-text search runs locally with no API call and no rate-limit cost.
